_doc: How each corpus is served and scored, so a measurement in docs/eval/EVAL.md is reproduced by one command: python dev_tools/eval/eval_corpus.py <corpus>. `bundle` is relative to $RAVEL_ROOT (default ../Ravel): the Ravel bundle the database was prepared from, whose corpus.bm25.json is the vocabulary the engine and harness read. `db` is the prepared Postgres volume and the container and host port that serve it; a missing volume is made with `ravel db prepare <bundle> --dsn ...` into a fresh vera-db:pg16-rum-bm25. `db.schema`, when set, is the schema the corpus lives in inside a database that holds several (unified mode, SCALING.md §4a); unset, it is the database's own `public`. `domains`, when set, is a file in config/ listing every domain one engine serves (DOMAINS_FILE); the corpus's `schema` then only tells the harness where this question set's labels live. `algorithms` is a file in config/. `engine` is environment the engine container is started with. Every other engine knob runs at its docker-compose.yml default: compose reads eval.env, never the operator's .env. The password is $EVAL_DB_PASSWORD, else POSTGRES_PASSWORD from .env; it is never printed.

id_reg_markdown.measured: docs/eval/EVAL.md; the fresh split is EVAL_SPLIT=fresh

id_reg_unified.measured: SCALING.md §5 step 3b: id_reg_markdown's tables, moved into schema id_reg of the unified database

unified_id_reg.measured: SCALING.md §5 step 3c: the Indonesian questions through one engine serving every domain in config/domains.unified.json

unified_ca_laws.measured: SCALING.md §5 step 3c: the Canadian questions through one engine serving every domain in config/domains.unified.json

ca_laws_unified.measured: SCALING.md §5 step 3c: ca_laws prepared by Ravel into schema ca_laws of the unified database
